title: World Literature Library
description: Explore great stories from around the world — from classic children's tales to young adult literature from every continent.

books.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.summary: Alice falls down a rabbit hole into a bizarre fantasy world populated by peculiar creatures, a Mad Hatter, a Cheshire Cat, and a tyrannical Queen of Hearts.
discussion: Why does Carroll mix sense and nonsense throughout the story?
How does Alice change from the beginning to the end?

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, must survive encounters with the bear Baloo, the panther Bagheera, and the tiger Shere Khan.
discussion: Does Mowgli truly belong with the wolves or with humans?
What does the Law of the Jungle represent?

books.title: The Little Prince
books.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
books.summary: A young prince travels from his tiny asteroid to Earth, meeting various characters. The story explores themes of loneliness, friendship, love, and the loss of childlike wonder in adulthood.
discussion: What does the fox mean when he says 'What is essential is invisible to the eye'?
Why do grown-ups 'never understand anything by themselves'?

books.title: Matilda
books.author: Roald Dahl
books.summary: Matilda is a brilliant child with neglectful parents and an abusive headmistress, Miss Trunchbull. She discovers she has telekinetic powers and uses them to fight back.
discussion: How does reading help Matilda escape her difficult life?
Is it ever right to break the rules like Matilda does?

books.title: The Wind in the Willows
books.author: Kenneth Grahame
books.summary: The adventures of four friends — Mole, Rat, Badger, and the irrepressible Mr Toad — along the banks of an English river.
discussion: What does 'home' mean to Mole in the story?
Is Mr Toad likeable despite his faults? Why?

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.summary: Young Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map and sails to a remote island with a crew that includes the cunning Long John Silver, searching for buried pirate gold.
discussion: Is Long John Silver a villain or an anti-hero?
What does Jim learn about trust?

books.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.summary: Dorothy is swept by a tornado to the magical land of Oz, where she must find the great Wizard to help her return home. She is joined by the Scarecrow, Tin Man, and Cowardly Lion.
discussion: Each character thinks they lack something. Do they really?
What is the significance of 'There's no place like home'?

books.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
books.author: Carlo Collodi
books.summary: A wooden puppet named Pinocchio is brought to life and goes on adventures, always getting into trouble because of his disobedience, lying, and foolishness — but yearning to become a real boy.
discussion: Why does lying have consequences in this story?
What does it mean to 'become a real boy'?

books.title: One Thousand and One Nights
books.author: Various / Traditional
books.summary: A collection of Middle Eastern folk tales told by Scheherazade to delay her execution. Stories include Aladdin, Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, and Sinbad the Sailor.
discussion: Why is storytelling powerful in this collection?
What makes Scheherazade a hero?

books.title: Anansi the Spider
books.author: West African Oral Tradition
books.summary: Anansi is a spider who uses cleverness and trickery to outwit larger, more powerful animals. He is a cultural hero of the Akan people of Ghana and Caribbean folklore.
discussion: What makes Anansi a good role model despite his tricks?
Why do you think spider stories spread across the African diaspora?

books.title: Panchatantra
books.author: Vishnu Sharma (attributed)
books.summary: The Panchatantra is an ancient Indian collection of interlinked animal fables with moral lessons, written in Sanskrit. It has influenced Aesop's Fables and La Fontaine.
discussion: What is the difference between wisdom and cleverness?
Which fable's lesson do you find most useful in your own life?

books.title: Cinderella: Variations Around the World
books.author: Various
books.summary: The Cinderella story type exists in over 500 versions worldwide: Yeh-Shen (China, 9th century), Aschenputtel (Germany, Grimm), Cendrillon (France, Perrault), Anklet for a Princess (India), Domitila (Mexico). Each reflects its culture's values.
discussion: How does each culture's version reflect its values?
Is the Cinderella story feminist or anti-feminist?

books.title: Anne of Green Gables
books.author: L.M. Montgomery
books.summary: Spirited, red-haired orphan Anne Shirley is mistakenly sent to elderly siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert in Prince Edward Island, Canada. Her imagination, intelligence, and warmth slowly win everyone's hearts.
discussion: How does Anne's imagination help and hinder her?
What does belonging mean to Anne?

books.title: The Secret Garden
books.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
books.summary: Mary Lennox, a spoilt orphan sent to live in a Yorkshire manor, discovers a locked secret garden and helps it grow again — along with her own transformation.
discussion: How does the garden mirror the changes in Mary?
What role does nature play in mental wellbeing?

books.title: The Diary of a Young Girl
books.author: Anne Frank
books.summary: The real diary of Anne Frank, a Jewish girl who hid with her family in Amsterdam for two years during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands during World War II. A profound and moving account of humanity, hope, and resilience.
discussion: How does Anne maintain hope in such terrible circumstances?
What does this diary teach us about human resilience?

books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.summary: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit who wants no adventures, is swept into a quest with a company of dwarves and the wizard Gandalf to reclaim their mountain home from the dragon Smaug.
discussion: How does Bilbo change during the journey?
What is Tolkien saying about greed through the character of Smaug?

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.author: Harper Lee
books.summary: Scout Finch narrates her childhood in 1930s Alabama, where her father Atticus defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime. A defining novel about racial injustice, empathy, and moral courage.
discussion: What does Atticus mean when he says to climb into someone's skin and walk around in it?
What is the symbolism of the mockingbird?

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.summary: Amir, a wealthy Pashtun boy, and Hassan, his Hazara servant and friend, grow up together in Kabul. After a devastating betrayal, Amir's guilt follows him to America and back to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan.
discussion: Is redemption possible after a great betrayal?
How does the setting of Afghanistan affect the story?

books.title: Where the Sidewalk Ends
books.author: Shel Silverstein
books.summary: A beloved collection of poems and drawings for children, mixing playfulness, humour, and unexpected wisdom. Topics include imagination, friendship, and the joy of being different.
discussion: Pick a favourite poem and explain why it speaks to you.
How does Silverstein use humour to teach serious lessons?

books.title: Rumi: Selected Poems
books.author: Jalal ad-Din Rumi
books.summary: The 13th-century Persian poet Rumi wrote some of the most beautiful and profound poetry in world literature, exploring themes of love, longing, the divine, and the human soul. His Masnavi is considered the greatest work of Sufi literature.
discussion: What does Rumi mean by 'the reed flute' in his most famous poem?
Why has Rumi's poetry resonated across 800 years and cultures?
